 The sunscreen that works with your make-up this spring
 Face first
 3 min read November 19, 2026 - 8:00AM Advertiser content.
 Sun protection is an important part of any Aussie’s skincare routine. Who says it can’t be a seamless one, too? 
 As sunny conditions start heating up across Australia, the ultimate beauty flex isn’t simply a flawless face base – it’s protecting your skin without compromising your make-up finish.
 The age-old dilemma of sunscreen that slips, pills or leaves a chalky white cast ends here, thanks to a skin-savvy sunscreen formula, which is formulated to offer both broad-spectrum sun protection and skincare benefits.
 The spring skincare mistake ruining your foundation
 Spring often influences our make-up like it does our wardrobe choices – seeing us swapping out the heavy layers for a lighter, fresher take.
 Softer, dewier finishes and glowy radiance become the new goals, at a time when the calendar starts filling with sunny brunches, outdoor weddings and other al fresco events.
 We all know the importance of sun protection, especially in Australia.
 Yet the awkward finish and texture of some sunscreens still sees some women skipping this key daily skincare step.
 So how do you get your sunscreen to work in harmony with the rest of your beauty routine?
 How to layer sunscreen and make-up
 Sunscreen is most effective when it’s properly applied. [1] 
 Here are some tips [2] for incorporating it into your morning routine:
 #1. Apply sunscreen 20 minutes before sun exposure
 #2. Sunscreen is best applied to clean, dry skin
 #3. Use about one teaspoon of sunscreen across your face and neck, spreading evenly to cover
 #4. Allow sunscreen a few minutes to settle into the skin before following with make-up [3] 
 How do you reapply sunscreen during the day?
 Aim to reapply your sunscreen every two hours, or straight after any sweating, swimming or towel-drying. [4] 
 But juggling that process without disrupting your make-up can be easier said than done.
 For a smoother result, a lightweight sunscreen formula is often easier to blend and less likely to clash with your foundation or base.  
 Finding a fast-absorbing product with an invisible finish can also help.
 To reapply sunscreen, you can gently pat the product on to your face over the top of your make-up. [5] 
 Finally, don’t skimp on sunscreen!
 Find a sunscreen you like enough to use on repeat, and both your skin and your make-up will thank you.
 Loading embed... Meet the Avène Sunsitive sunscreen range
 For very high, broad-spectrum UVB-UVA protection that works with your beauty routine, rather than against it, consider Avène’s face-friendly Sunsitive sunscreen range, created with the Australian sun in mind.
 Avène Sunsitive Sunscreen Fluid SPF50+ is a lightweight formula for the face, providing four hours of water resistance [6] and a sensitive-skin formulation that also comes with vitamin E and aloe vera for additional skin benefits.
 With a fast-absorbing, invisible finish, it sits effortlessly under make-up, making it the ideal beauty bag staple.
 There is one bottle of the sunscreen sold in Australian pharmacies every 90 seconds. [7] 
 To pair your protection with a hydrated glow, Avène Sunsitive Sunscreen Serum SPF50+ is an ultra-lightweight serum designed for sensitive skin.
 Containing hyaluronic acid, vitamin E and aloe vera, this formula leaves skin feeling hydrated, reducing the need for multiple pre-sunscreen skincare steps.
 It’s quick to absorb and leaves a soft, dewy finish, working as the ideal base for spring make-up looks.
 How your sunscreen purchase can support sun safety and the Melanoma & Skin Cancer Advocacy Network
 This year, Avène is throwing its support behind the Melanoma & Skin Cancer Advocacy Network (MSCAN), an Australian charity dedicated to driving policy reform, supporting clinical research and providing resources for people affected by melanoma and skin cancer.
 For every Avène Sunsitive Sunscreen product purchased, Avène will donate $1 to MSCAN to fund research, advocate for better care for people affected by skin cancer and spread knowledge about skin checks.
